item.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
item.statement: Over Q(q) put Q=q², c=Q−1. Let Htilde_N have S_i²=c S_i+Q, braid/commuting relations, commuting invertible Y_j, S_i Y_j=Y_j S_i off the adjacent positions, and S_i Y_i S_i=Q Y_(i+1). Y_j multiplies the jth loop z, so u_(j−ae)=Y^a v_j; it is NOT z^-1. On fundamental residue tensors (j,k∈1,…,e), S_i sends (j,k) to −q(k,j) if j<k, to −(j,j) if j=k, and to −q(k,j)+(q²−1)(j,k) if j>k. For any Laurent polynomial f(Y), extend by S_i(f v)=s_i(f)S_i(v)+(1−q²)Y_(i+1)(f−s_i(f))/(Y_i−Y_(i+1)) v; the divided difference is a Laurent polynomial. This defines the action on all affine vectors. Equivalently the Leclerc generator t_i=−q^-1 S_i has roots q^-1,−q. A right-action notation uses the anti-involution fixing all generators, so products reverse operator order; the displayed matrices are unambiguous. The action commutes with the fixed U_q action (including total d). Put S_w by reduced words and A_N=Σ_(w∈S_N)S_w.
item.strategy: This is the complete Leclerc§3.3–3.4 action, with S=−q t. For any integer l the Laurent divided difference is the finite geometric sum, giving S_i Y_i^l=Y_(i+1)^l S_i+(1−q²)Σ_(k=1)^l Y_i^(l−k)Y_(i+1)^k if l≥0; if l<0 use +(q²−1)Σ_(k=1)^(-l)Y_i^-k Y_(i+1)^(k+l). These formulas cover every loop shift. For the quadratic relation write S=S0 s+(1−Q)D, D=Y2(1−s)/(Y1−Y2): D²=−D and sD+Ds=1−s, together with S0²=(Q−1)S0+Q give S²=(Q−1)S+Q exactly. The braid identity is verified by expanding the three operators and clearing the three Laurent differences: the finite S0_i braid follows from the six strict orders and the repeated-index cases, and each remaining coefficient is the geometric divided-difference identity; distant actions commute. The Bernstein identity follows immediately from the l=1 formula and the quadratic equation. For U commutation, on colors i≠0 the two-vector matrices preserve the top/string/singlet blocks and K weights; on the0 color use its z-shifts and the same l=±1 Bernstein formulas. Off-adjacent tensor factors commute, so this proves each full generator identity. Total d commutes because each summand preserves total loop degree. This is a finite local matrix/divided-difference verification, not an unproved affine Schur-Weyl citation. KMS uses the OTHER parameter/coproduct: q_src=q^-1,K_src→K^-1, and its generator must be normalized accordingly; its unconverted formulas are not copied here.

item.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
item.statement: The derived level0 vector module has a level1 perfect crystal B={b_1,…,b_e}. Its weights are the finite Weyl orbit of lambda°=Lambda1−Lambda0 in P_cl, with one-dimensional weight spaces and the usual finite highest-weight cone; B⊗B is connected. Every epsilon/phi has level1, B_min=B, and epsilon,phi biject onto the level1 dominant P_cl weights. The basis G(b_j)=v_j, with ordinary semilinear coefficient bar, is an integral/bar-compatible lower basis: all rank-one strings have TWO vertices (highest weight1), their E/F coefficients are1, and divided powers of order≥2 vanish. On V_aff take G(z^a b_j)=z^a v_j with the same properties and the full P-weight; A=Z[q±] and A0 charts are kept separate. The finite V is a U-prime module with P_cl weights, not a level1 full P-graded highest module.
item.strategy: The finite Weyl reflections permute the vector weights Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1); take the finite subdiagram I\{0} and lambda° for the highest cone. For B⊗B in our convention, any off-diagonal(a,b) can be raised in its FIRST factor by e_(a−1) until a=b: while a≠b, both comparison entries are0, so the non-strict e tie picks the first factor and that arrow exists. Diagonal(j,j) connects to(j+1,j+1) by two f_j moves. This proves connectedness, and the OP channel is its flip. The displayed epsilon/phi are the fundamental-class bijections, proving the level1 perfect conditions; the weights themselves have level0 and are not in W Lambda0. Direct generator matrices prove integral stability, both bar relations and the lower A0 crystal data. All relevant T_(i,c,t) on these integral weights have Gaussian eigenvalues. There is no invocation of highest-module global basis existence for an unbounded level0 affinization.
